items.statement_scope: Whole original16.59: for every finite group K, does a finite group G exist with K isomorphic to Out(G)=Aut(G)/Inn(G)? The selected YCor answer constructs a finite semidirect product for each finite group Q. The pre-existing realization by an infinite group is context, and the other MO answers are not counted as new questions.

standard_prerequisites: Finite free nilpotent Lie algebras with multigrading and their finite-dimensional quotients.
Malcev-Lazard/Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff correspondence in nilpotency class c<p, as explicitly used in the author construction on physical4.
Coprime Hall-complement conjugacy and automorphism factor structure for products of directly indecomposable center-free groups, as used in Lemma2 and Proposition1.
